title: fix(components,plugin-view): forward the row-click modifier payload to the host
body:
Fixes #9462

`Clause-2: yes` — and the mechanical floor is NOT the reading here. A `^\+export`
count over this diff is **0**, because nothing new is exported: the widening lands
on `ObjectViewProps.onRowClick`, a parameter on a type that
`packages/plugin-view/src/index.tsx` already re-exports from the package entry
(`export type { ObjectViewProps } from './ObjectView';`), and `plugin-view` is not
private with its `exports["."]` types condition pointing at `./dist/index.d.ts`.
So a published declaration MOVES. ⛔ Do not read that `0` as a clearance.

## What changed

`useNavigationOverlay`'s `handleClick` has always invoked the handler it is given
with two arguments — the record, and the modifier payload (`metaKey` / `ctrlKey` /
`button`). objectui#9360 made the hook's option declare the payload; objectui#9460
made the component props on the path declare it. Three hops in the middle received
it and passed one argument on, so a host wiring Cmd/Ctrl/middle-click read
`undefined` as its second argument and "open in a new tab" silently degraded to an
ordinary navigation.

1. `packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx`, the row's own click
   handler — was `schema.onRowClick(row)`, now `schema.onRowClick(row, e)`.
2. The same file's hover "open record" button — was `schema.onRowClick?.(row)`, now
   `schema.onRowClick?.(row, e)`. This is the interesting one: its handler had
   already bound the DOM event as `e` to call `stopPropagation`, so the payload was
   **in scope on that line** and still was not handed on.
3. `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` — `handleRowClick` was truncating to
   `onRowClick(record)`, now forwards `onRowClick(record, event)`. Its own branches
   deliberately do not READ the event: what a modifier click should do when no host
   handler is present is the hook's decision, taken before this callback runs.

⛔ The payload's contents are untouched — `metaKey` / `ctrlKey` / `button` is
objectui#9360's declaration. This is a forward, not a redefinition.

## The three reds, and the control, in one file

`packages/app-shell/src/__tests__/rowClickModifierPayloadForward-9462.test.tsx`.
It lives in `app-shell` because that is the one package that already depends on
all four subjects, so the control can share the file without a new dependency
edge anywhere — and because `app-shell` is the real host: its own views already
spell their row-click handlers with two parameters.

RED-FIRST, measured twice — once on the first commit and again after merging
`main` (the second run also proves the ablation still bites with the sibling
data-table change from objectui#9623 present). Method: revert the three source
files to the branch point, prove the mutation reached the disk by counting the
injected and the removed text in both directions, run, then restore from `HEAD`
and prove the restore by blob hash rather than by an exit code.

| case | on the mutated tree |
|---|---|
| RED 1 — ⌘-click a row through `ObjectGrid` | `expected undefined to be defined` |
| RED 2 — Ctrl-click the hover "open record" button | `expected undefined to be defined` |
| RED 3 — `ObjectView`'s own `onRowClick` prop | `expected undefined to be defined` |
| ⭐ CONTROL — ⌘-click an `ObjectGallery` card | **GREEN**, both before and after |

The control is `ObjectGallery`, which already forwards
(`navigation.handleClick(item, e)`). It is what separates "these three hops drop
the payload" from "the harness never delivered `metaKey`" — without it, a broken
probe produces exactly the same three failures.

The consumer-arity ledger
(`packages/react/src/hooks/__tests__/navigationOverlayConsumers.onRowClickArity-9357.test.ts`)
went red on the same run, which is the handshake it was built for: two of its
CONTROLS were OUT on a claim about BEHAVIOUR ("this hop hands over one argument,
so widening the declaration would promise a payload that never arrives"), and
repairing the hops made those same declarations understated. They moved into
`IN_SITES` rather than being edited in place.

## Declarations widened — and the one deliberately not

Widened, because the call they receive now carries the payload:

- `DataTableSchema.onRowClick` (`packages/types/src/data-display.ts`) — required,
  not optional: the renderer's two call sites do not compile against a
  one-parameter declaration.
- `ObjectViewProps.onRowClick` (`packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`) — the
  published one, see the clause-2 note above.
- The `onRowClick` inside `ObjectViewProps.renderListView`'s props — that is
  `handleRowClick` handed verbatim to a host's custom list view.

Each second parameter is optional and spelled `any`, for the reason objectui#9341
measured on `ObjectKanbanSchema.onCardClick`: `HandleClickModifiers` lives in
`@object-ui/react`, which depends on `@object-ui/types`, so naming it there is a
phantom dependency and closes a cycle — and a host that discovered the payload
from the implementation annotated it as React's mouse event, which a narrower
declaration refuses contravariantly. Source-compatible in both directions: no
existing handler is refused, and none is forced to take the second argument.

⛔ **NOT widened, and reported instead:** `ObjectDataTableSchema.onRowClick`
(`packages/types/src/objectql.ts`). `ObjectDataTable` in `plugin-dashboard` puts
`schema.onRowClick ?? handleRowClick` on the same `data-table` node, so after this
change a host handler on that key IS invoked with the payload while the
declaration still says one parameter — a live instance of objectui#9357's class,
one hop further out. It is out of this card's pinned scope, so it stays a control
in the arity ledger with its justification rewritten to state the gap rather than
claim accuracy, and it is reported for its own card.

## Verification

Every command below ran from the repo root; the heavy ones went through the shared
serialisation lock in the sibling `objectstack` checkout.

- `turbo run type-check` for `@object-ui/types`, `@object-ui/components`,
  `@object-ui/plugin-view` — 19/19 tasks successful (this also builds the
  dependency closure, so the `.d.ts` the checks read are freshly built).
- `turbo run type-check` for `@object-ui/react`, `@object-ui/app-shell` —
  31/31 tasks successful.
- `turbo run lint` for all five of those packages — 6/6 tasks successful,
  **0 errors** (the warning counts each package prints are pre-existing and
  repo-wide).
- `vitest run` over `packages/plugin-view/`, `packages/types/`,
  `packages/react/src/hooks/` and the new pin — 274 files / 5439 tests green.
- `vitest run` over `packages/components/`, `packages/plugin-grid/`,
  `packages/plugin-list/`, `packages/plugin-dashboard/`, `packages/plugin-detail/`
  — 796 files / 7841 tests green. ⚠️ This one was measured BEFORE the `main`
  merge; the post-merge re-run below is narrowed, and CI owns the full farm.
- Post-merge re-run at `dea7eb802`: `packages/components/src/renderers/complex/`,
  every `packages/components/src/__tests__/data-table*` file, `packages/plugin-view/`,
  `packages/react/src/hooks/__tests__/` and the new pin — 98 files / 886 tests green.
- Gates, all exit 0 on the merged head: `check:control-bytes`,
  `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check:handler-key-reads`,
  `check:phantom-deps`, `check:unreferenced-sources`,
  `check-changeset-presence.mjs`. Earlier on the same branch, also exit 0:
  `check:self-import`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`,
  `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:changeset-claims`,
  `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`,
  `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`.
- `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over every changed path: NOT GOVERNED.

⚠️ One narrowing, declared rather than hidden: an argument-level scan for tests
that pin the row-click call's exact argument list
(`toHaveBeenCalledWith` / `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` / `toHaveBeenLastCalledWith`
in any file mentioning `onRowClick` or `handleRowClick`) found exactly one, the
hook's own two-argument assertion, which is unaffected. That is the failure mode
an added argument has, and it was searched for directly instead of being left to
a full-repo run.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope, noted and NOT filed:

- `packages/plugin-grid/src/VirtualGrid.tsx` declares
  `onRowClick?: (row: any, index: number) => void` — a different contract with a
  different second parameter, already pinned as a control in the arity ledger.
  Not on this path. Successor: the arity ledger already carries it.
- `packages/fields/src/widgets/RecordPickerDialog.tsx` declares a one-parameter
  `onRowClick` on its custom-table render prop. It is the picker's own contract
  and never reaches the `data-table` slot. Successor: none.
- `packages/plugin-designer/src/ObjectManager.tsx` passes a one-parameter handler
  to `ObjectGrid`'s two-parameter prop. Assignable, and it simply ignores the
  payload — a choice, not a defect. Successor: none.

To file (one finding, three classes checked — class (b), a published declaration
that understates a real call):

- `ObjectDataTableSchema.onRowClick` in `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` still
  declares one parameter while the `data-table` channel it feeds now delivers two.
  Dedupe words: `ObjectDataTableSchema`, `onRowClick`, `modifier payload`,
  `arity`, `ObjectDataTable`. objectui#9357 is not addressed here and objectui#9460
  is not addressed here; this is a successor to both.
